title: Accelerating DTCO with a Sample-Efficient Active Learning Framework for TCAD Device Modeling
problem: Neural Compact Models require substantial training data, and TCAD simulations are time-intensive and expensive. The challenge is to accurately model device behavior while minimizing the number of required TCAD simulations.
motivation: Accelerating DTCO through efficient device modeling reduces design time and cost, enabling faster chip design optimization.
method: The framework uses active learning—strategically picking simulations rather than running them randomly. It ranks candidate simulations by three factors: model uncertainty (measured using the neural tangent kernel, a mathematical tool for estimating confidence in predictions), simulation time, and I-V curve complexity (how variable the device's behavior is). By prioritizing highly uncertain simulations where the model has the most to learn, the framework reduces the total number of expensive TCAD simulations while maintaining accuracy.
key_novelty: Using neural tangent kernel-based uncertainty to select which TCAD device simulations to run reduces the total number of simulations needed to train accurate device models.
contributions: Active Learning framework for reducing simulation count in NCM-based device modeling
Ranking algorithm combining NTK variance, simulation time, and I-V curve complexity metrics
